title: Midwest diesel rises 6.9% in a second consecutive weekly jump
summary: EIA’s 21 September Midwest diesel benchmark is $6.680/gal, up $0.430 from $6.250 (+6.9%) after the prior week’s 5.1% rise. The prior public escalation trigger was crossed; Watershed’s actual carrier surcharge, lane mix and pass-through remain unknown.
factorRationale: Exposure 75: public facility geography makes truck freight plausible, but mode and miles are unmeasured. Severity 80: the benchmark reached $6.680/gal and rose 6.9% in one week. Confidence 70: primary EIA measurement, with no company contract or invoice. Persistence 80: two consecutive weekly increases above 5%, supported by the separate EIA distillate-constraint scenario. Velocity 80: weekly repricing can reach surcharges quickly. Dependency 80 and substitutability 35: road freight is operationally important and near-term fuel substitution is limited, but actual carrier terms are unknown.
causalPath: Regional retail diesel benchmark ↑ → applicable carrier fuel surcharge or freight quote ↑ → delivered input/outbound cost and conditional margin or service pressure.
verify: Current carrier surcharge tables and invoices, contract lag, lane and mode mix, outbound miles, customer pass-through and any tender or service refusal.
action: CFO and Supply Chain should reconcile current carrier surcharge tables and invoices, estimate next-cycle margin and OTIF exposure, and confirm customer pass-through before new commitments.
trigger: A third consecutive >5% weekly rise, actual contracted transport cost >5% above plan, a tender/service refusal, or a verified customer-service impact.
dateNote: EIA released the data on 22 September 2026; the price reference week is 21 September. This is a regional retail benchmark, not a Watershed freight rate or realized loss.
coverageChange: Crossed the prior public trigger: a second consecutive weekly rise above 5%. Guidance changes to immediate invoice/contract verification; no realized company loss or urgent continuity event is asserted.

title: Grain outlook tightens; specialty basis still unknown
summary: September WASDE projects U.S. total-grain ending stocks of 62.92 Mt versus 65.03 Mt in August. That is a broad context signal, not a popcorn forecast.
factorRationale: Broad grain balance → potential feed/grain pricing → formula costs. All seven factors are uncalibrated proxies (45/55/45/80/45/55/60); popping-grade corn and food-grade contracts can diverge materially.
causalPath: Broad grain balance → potential feed/grain pricing → formula costs. All seven factors are uncalibrated proxies (45/55/45/80/45/55/60); popping-grade corn and food-grade contracts can diverge materially.
verify: Actual grains, specification basis, origin, contracts and inventory cover.
action: Track supplier quotations before changing coverage or formulations.
trigger: Two relevant supplier quotes worsen >10%, or verified cover falls below the approved operating threshold.

title: Traceability planning requires a product-form decision
summary: FDA describes a proposed extension and a congressional direction not to enforce the rule before 20 July 2028. Applicability still depends on covered food and form.
factorRationale: Covered receiving/transformation → KDE/CTE obligations → systems and partner coordination. Scope is not established for Watershed; factors 55/65/65/90/25/70/60 reflect planning exposure rather than a violation.
causalPath: Covered receiving/transformation → KDE/CTE obligations → systems and partner coordination. Scope is not established for Watershed; factors 55/65/65/90/25/70/60 reflect planning exposure rather than a violation.
verify: Food Traceability List applicability at each process stage; exemptions; customer contractual dates.
action: Quality and IT should map covered inputs and data exchanges, retaining product-specific legal review.
trigger: Final regulatory change, customer deadline, or a confirmed gap in an applicable traceability process.

title: Pet formats offer a qualified commercial opening
summary: APPA projects $69.7bn of pet-food and treat sales for 2026. This does not establish unit growth or freeze-dried segment growth.
factorRationale: Pet-category spending → candidate launch budgets → topper/inclusion projects suited to advertised capabilities. Factors 70/60/45/85/45/65/65 reflect an unvalidated sales hypothesis, not Watershed revenue.
causalPath: Pet-category spending → candidate launch budgets → topper/inclusion projects suited to advertised capabilities. Factors 70/60/45/85/45/65/65 reflect an unvalidated sales hypothesis, not Watershed revenue.
verify: Premium segment units, brand launch plans, current capacity and qualified process fit.
action: Build a small list of qualified topper/inclusion prospects and test demand before reserving capacity.
trigger: Documented customer briefs and trial conversion, with confirmed available capacity and validated safety controls.
dateNote: APPA projection publication date unverified; baseline evidence, not a new event on retrieval day.

title: Popcorn expansion is an opportunity to verify
summary: Deer Creek’s public directory now lists Aunt Em’s / Heartland together. The reported equipment transition remains unverified as completed.
factorRationale: Announced process additions → possible new formats → private-label prospects. Factors 70/65/60/85/40/75/60 assume qualification work; no incremental capacity is counted as operational.
causalPath: Announced process additions → possible new formats → private-label prospects. Factors 70/65/60/85/40/75/60 assume qualification work; no incremental capacity is counted as operational.
verify: Equipment ownership, commissioning, production qualification and available slots.
action: Confirm the production milestone before offering new formats or delivery commitments.
trigger: Verified commissioned capacity plus a qualified customer opportunity.

title: Baby-food lead guidance has a material scope exclusion
summary: The FDA final guidance excludes grain-based and freeze-dried snacks. It must not be applied automatically to every toddler product.
factorRationale: SKU classification → applicable contaminant requirements/customer specifications → testing and release criteria. Low velocity 20 reflects an existing rule, not new contamination. Other factors are analytical prioritization.
causalPath: SKU classification → applicable contaminant requirements/customer specifications → testing and release criteria. Low velocity 20 reflects an existing rule, not new contamination. Other factors are analytical prioritization.
verify: Each SKU’s form, age positioning, state rules and customer specifications.
action: Keep contaminant controls; have Quality document the correct guidance scope by SKU.
trigger: Changed FDA/state requirements or an actual out-of-spec result; then use the approved food-safety response process.

title: Central Illinois storm risk is tapering; no facility-county alert matched
summary: The 21 September NWS outlook includes McLean, Woodford and Tazewell counties, but says showers and thunderstorms are concentrated especially near and south of I-72, will taper by early afternoon, and are not expected to become severe. Lightning remains possible. The 14:16 UTC collector snapshot contained no active alert matched to the three Illinois county SAME codes, and no facility disruption is established.
factorRationale: Exposure falls from 85 to 60 because the county-zone outlook includes the three public municipalities while activity is concentrated especially near and south of I-72, south of the confirmed municipalities; severity falls from 55 to 35 because NWS says severe storms are not expected but lightning remains possible; confidence remains 80 because the primary outlook and SAME-code check are current while site impact is unknown; persistence falls from 40 to 25 because storms are expected to taper by early afternoon and no hazards are expected Tuesday through Sunday; velocity remains 80 because any effect is same-day; dependency and substitutability remain 70/70 pending actual shift, route and scheduling information. These are provisional judgments, not measured disruption.
causalPath: County-zone showers and lightning → possible brief local road, workforce or outdoor-activity interruption → dispatch and production continuity. The forecast concentration is south of the confirmed municipalities, and actual route, utility and site effects remain unverified.
verify: Current county warnings, lightning proximity, verified route closures, dispatch timing and site conditions. The exact Top Fox production allocation remains unknown.
action: No additional response is supported beyond normal weather procedures and checking current site and route conditions before affected dispatch or outdoor work.
trigger: A warning matching an operating location, verified route closure, utility interruption or reported site impact warrants immediate reassessment and the approved continuity response.
dateNote: NWS issued 04:07 CDT on 21 September. The 14:16 UTC collector snapshot contained no active alert matching Illinois SAME codes 017113, 017203 or 017179. Factors changed only where the new forecast supports lower exposure, severity and persistence; guidance is improving without an operating-clearance claim.

title: Ingredient benchmarks diverge: grains up, dairy down
summary: August BLS PPI: grains +4.3% and oilseeds +3.9% month over month (SA); dairy products -1.0% (NSA). These broad benchmarks cannot be netted into a Watershed cost change without actual purchasing weights.
factorRationale: Exposure 60: advertised platforms imply plausible input channels, not measured spend. Severity 50: material benchmark moves with offsets. Confidence 60: primary data but unknown purchase basis. Persistence 65: possible contract lag; velocity 50: one monthly observation. Dependency 65: ingredient relevance; substitutability 65: broad alternatives subject to quality/customer approval. All factors are provisional judgments.
causalPath: Grain/oilseed and dairy benchmark divergence → category-specific vendor quotes and contract resets → conditional product margins.
verify: Actual ingredient basket, food-grade specifications, quote dates, contract basis, inventory cover and customer pass-through.
action: Compare the next quotes for grain, seed and dairy categories separately; quantify net effect only after purchasing weights are supplied.
trigger: A relevant delivered quote rises >5% against plan or confirmed pass-through fails to offset a sustained input increase.
dateNote: Reference August 2026; July-to-August changes. Preliminary. Oilseeds are not a pumpkin-seed quote; grains are not a food-grade popcorn quote.
coverageChange: Newly assessed coverage; not evidence that the event began on retrieval day.

title: Metro labor context remains mixed
summary: July preliminary NSA unemployment: Bloomington 3.3% (June 4.0%), Peoria 3.8% (4.5%), Milwaukee-Waukesha 3.8% (3.8%). Bloomington and Peoria manufacturing employment was 1.2% and 0.9% below a year earlier. This does not establish a Watershed shortage.
factorRationale: Exposure 65: relevant regional operating presence. Severity 45: labor-market context without company vacancies. Confidence 45 in the conditional channel, reduced by metro aggregation and seasonality. Persistence 65 and velocity 30: lagged monthly data. Dependency 65: manufacturing staffing. Substitutability 65: unmeasured local alternatives. These are judgments, not a shortage estimate.
causalPath: Regional hiring conditions → conditional recruitment and retention difficulty → staffing, throughput and overtime.
verify: Time to fill by trade and site, accepted wage rates, overtime, turnover, vacancy counts and actual recruiting catchments.
action: Use metro data to frame a hiring review; compare it with actual recruiting results before changing staffing or pay assumptions.
trigger: Critical maintenance/production roles remain unfilled >45 days or persistent overtime exceeds the approved site plan.
dateNote: Reference July 2026, preliminary and not seasonally adjusted. Exact release day unverified; retrieved September 17. Monthly declines can be seasonal.
coverageChange: Newly assessed coverage; not evidence that the event began on retrieval day.

title: National industrial electricity benchmark rises 4.7% year over year
summary: EIA’s 24 September release reports a July 2026 U.S. industrial average revenue of 9.77 cents/kWh, 4.7% above July 2025. This national proxy replaces an expired June state snapshot for coverage; it is not a Watershed tariff, bill or state-level comparison.
factorRationale: Exposure 80: Watershed advertises energy-dependent processing platforms, but kWh and tariffs are unknown. Severity 50: the national industrial benchmark is 4.7% higher year over year. Confidence 60: primary EIA data, discounted because a national average does not establish Illinois, Wisconsin or facility billing. Persistence 70: monthly cost-planning relevance without proof of contract reset. Velocity 35: lagged July data. Dependency 90: process energy is necessary. Substitutability 40: near-term process-energy alternatives may be limited, while tariff and efficiency options are unverified.
causalPath: National industrial electricity benchmark ↑ → possible applicable tariff or supply-contract reset → conditional processing and handling cost for freeze-dried, baked, roasted and popped platforms.
verify: Facility tariffs, demand charges, supply contracts, interval usage, effective cents/kWh, kWh per product and reset dates; no utility provider is assumed.
action: Finance and operations should compare actual effective cents/kWh and process energy use with plan; use the national series only as a screening benchmark.
trigger: Actual effective energy cost exceeds plan by >10% for two billing periods or an applicable utility/grid notice creates a verified continuity concern.
dateNote: EIA released July 2026 data on 24 September; national industrial average revenue per kWh is a price proxy. This revision is not directly comparable with the prior Illinois/Wisconsin June values.
coverageChange: A new national July benchmark restores energy coverage after the state snapshot expired. The measurement basis changed, so the lower model score is not evidence that Watershed energy exposure improved.

title: Packaging signals split between paperboard and plastics
summary: August PPI: paperboard +2.3% month over month (NSA) and +5.1% year over year; plastic resins -0.8% (SA); unsupported plastic film, sheet, and other shapes -0.5% (NSA), still +12.5% year over year. These categories are broader than food packaging.
factorRationale: Exposure 65: plausible film/carton dependence with specifications unknown. Severity 55: paperboard increase amid plastic monthly relief. Confidence 60: public indices but uncertain conversion into quotes. Persistence 65 and velocity 45: monthly changes and potential contract lag. Dependency 65: packaging requirement; substitutability 60: specification and customer approvals. Provisional analyst judgments.
causalPath: Paperboard/resin/converting cost changes → packaging vendor quotes and resets → conditional unit packaging cost and margins.
verify: Film structure, basis weight, print/conversion charges, carton specifications, resin/paperboard index clauses and contracted price lags.
action: Separate carton and film quote reviews; request evidence for index-linked adjustments rather than applying a blended packaging inflation rate.
trigger: Delivered packaging quotes exceed plan by >5% or a qualified vendor reports a material lead-time increase.
dateNote: Reference August 2026, preliminary. Annual and monthly changes are separate; the film series includes non-food shapes. Paperboard API is the same economic series, not independent corroboration.
coverageChange: Newly assessed coverage; not evidence that the event began on retrieval day.

title: Global CPG proxy shows mixed pet and snack demand with inventory pressure
summary: General Mills’ 23 September quarter reported North America Pet sales flat: pet treats grew low single digits, cat food double digits, dog food fell high single digits, and retailer inventory was a modest headwind. North America Retail organic sales fell 3% and U.S. Snacks declined mid-single digits. The company retained a cautious annual outlook while emphasizing protein, fiber and pet humanization. This is one archetype, not a Watershed customer or order signal.
factorRationale: Exposure 50: a relevant global CPG/pet archetype with no established Watershed account relationship. Severity 45: mixed category results and inventory pressure, not a confirmed order change. Confidence 70: primary quarterly disclosure, discounted for single-company and portfolio mismatch. Persistence 70: full-year outlook and inventory commentary. Velocity 35: quarterly evidence. Dependency 50: actual customer mix is unknown. Substitutability 70: multiple customer segments and platforms may diversify demand. Factors remain intentionally low for company impact.
causalPath: Archetype brand volumes, retailer inventories and innovation priorities → possible launch briefs, outsourcing appetite and order cadence → conditional Watershed sales pipeline.
verify: Actual customer segmentation; qualified briefs by pet treats, dog food, snacks, protein/fiber and other formats; retailer-inventory effects; pipeline stage; capacity and margin fit.
action: Sales and R&D should compare current qualified briefs with the mixed archetype signals, emphasizing validated pet-treat and protein/fiber problems while testing for snack or dog-food inventory drag before allocating capacity.
trigger: A verified customer changes orders, two additional primary archetypes corroborate the same volume/inventory move, or a qualified launch brief matches available capacity and validated controls.
dateNote: General Mills reported results on 23 September for the quarter ended 30 August 2026. Reported sales, organic sales and segment commentary are company-specific; no current Watershed customer relationship is inferred.
coverageChange: The scheduled quarterly recheck produced mixed demand evidence and specific innovation themes. Guidance changes from a generic cautious watch to category-by-category pipeline verification.

title: EIA’s export-constraint scenario supports a fuel watch
summary: EIA’s September outlook assumes Middle East export constraints through year-end and forecasts tight distillate inventories. This provides a conditional explanation for fuel exposure already tracked in S01, not a second independent loss estimate.
factorRationale: Exposure 65: global petroleum can affect domestic trucking without direct imports. Severity 70: distillate constraint scenario. Confidence 60: agency forecast, uncertain evolution. Persistence 80: year-end scenario; velocity 65: recent fuel moves. Dependency 75: conditional freight channel; substitutability 50: route/carrier choices do not fully replace diesel. Same fuel-cost issue group as S01; never added to it.
causalPath: Export/chokepoint constraints → global petroleum and distillate balance → domestic diesel benchmark → applicable carrier surcharge → delivered cost.
verify: Carrier surcharge formulas and lag, contractual pass-through, current EIA inventory releases and the assumptions behind the agency forecast; no Watershed import lane is asserted.
action: Use the same logistics/finance review as S01; run a conditional fuel-surcharge sensitivity instead of issuing a separate geopolitical alarm.
trigger: The observed relevant diesel benchmark or a contracted surcharge breaches the S01 trigger, or verified lane exposure changes.
dateNote: EIA forecast completed September 3 and released September 9. Projected inventories and export constraints are attributed scenarios, not realized measurements. No own forecast probability is created.
coverageChange: Newly assessed coverage; not evidence that the event began on retrieval day.
